entries.behavior: Across two clients under sustained large-object delete, put, get, and eviction pressure, every successful read returns the exact bytes most recently written for its key.
entries.reason: No discoverable Rust crate test currently sustains randomized cross-client delete/put/get operations with large values and eviction pressure.

entries.behavior: During repeated random crashes and restarts of a three-Master HA group, successful small-object puts remain readable with exact values, and service resumes for all keys after a surviving leader stabilizes.
entries.reason: No discoverable Rust crate test currently performs repeated randomized three-Master process crashes/restarts while asserting cross-client small-object availability and integrity.

entries.behavior: During repeated random crashes and restarts of a three-Master HA group under eviction-prone large-object pressure, every successful read preserves exact object bytes and stable surviving leaders resume service.
entries.reason: No discoverable Rust crate test currently combines randomized three-Master crash/restart cycles with large-object eviction pressure and cross-client byte-integrity assertions.

entries.behavior: An RPC bind host already expressed as a bare IPv4 address passes through unchanged and can start the RPC server.
entries.reason: Rust has segment-name routing normalization tests but no equivalent test that derives and binds the Client RPC host from a bare configured address.

entries.behavior: A configured IPv4 host with a data-plane port is stripped to the bare host before RPC server binding, allowing the server to start.
entries.reason: Rust has segment-name routing normalization tests but no equivalent assertion on Client RPC bind-host derivation and successful binding.

entries.behavior: Decimal and 0x/0X hexadecimal object keys parse as complete unsigned sequence hashes, while empty, malformed, and trailing-garbage keys are rejected.
A disabled KV-event publisher is a no-op for stored and removed notifications and leaves published and dropped counters at zero.
When the KV-event queue reaches capacity, the publisher drops the oldest event, retains newer events, and increments its dropped-event accounting.
Publishing an SGLang object key over ZMQ emits a three-frame message with sequence, stored event type, backend, tenant, group, object key, empty sequence hashes, and successful publish statistics.
Pinned-memory registration rejects duplicate and overlapping ranges while accepting an adjacent range, and each accepted range unregisters exactly once when released.
entries.reason: Rust implements overlap checks for owner-backed registrations but has no discoverable fake-native test proving duplicate/overlap rejection, adjacent acceptance, and exact unregister calls.

entries.behavior: Pinned-memory quota rejects capacity beyond the configured limit, releasing a region refunds capacity, and a later full-size registration succeeds and unregisters once.
entries.reason: Rust owner-backed registration has no equivalent configured pinned-byte quota test with release/refund accounting.

entries.behavior: A failed native pin operation refunds its reservation so retrying the same range after native recovery succeeds and later unregisters exactly once.
entries.reason: Rust has no discoverable fake-native regression test proving failed registration leaves no live or blocked reservation and permits an exact retry.

entries.behavior: A failed native unregister retains the address and quota reservation, preventing overlapping or capacity-consuming replacement registrations from reusing unsafe memory.
entries.reason: Rust records blocked ranges after Drop-time unregister failure, but no discoverable fake-native test proves the range remains unavailable after the failure.

entries.behavior: Copying host bytes to an accelerator pointer selects the matching device, switches to its device ordinal, performs a host-to-device copy, and preserves the bytes.
entries.reason: Rust FFI exposes copy_from_host but has no discoverable fake-device test for device selection, context switching, copy direction, and byte preservation.

entries.behavior: Copying from an accelerator pointer to host selects the matching device, switches to its device ordinal, performs a device-to-host copy, and preserves the bytes.
entries.reason: Rust FFI exposes copy_to_host but has no discoverable fake-device test for device selection, context switching, copy direction, and byte preservation.

entries.behavior: Pointer classification returns the accelerator device whose query reports device memory and preserves the reported device ordinal.
entries.reason: Rust tests raw pointer-kind enum decoding but not runtime device selection or preservation of a matching device ordinal.

entries.behavior: A null pointer is rejected before querying any accelerator device.
entries.reason: Rust classify_pointer delegates directly to native code and has no discoverable test proving null is rejected without a native device query.
